characters.name: Heathcliff "Cliff" Huxtable
characters.description: Amazingly Embarrassing Parent: Cliff seems tointentionallybe this most of the time when the children bring their dates or some other company to the house. Berserk Button: Don't say that Cliff would kick one of his children out of the house. When Denise tells him that she assumed he would kick her out if she dropped out of college, it's one of the only times in the show that we see him truly angry. Big Eater: Cliff loves junk food and will try to eat as much of it as he can if he thinks Clair won't find out. During the weekend before his annual physical, for example, he eats four large hoagies and half a strawberry cheesecake and washes them down with five large bottles of chocolate soda. Billed Above the Title: Bill Cosby inThe Cosby Show. Bumbling Dad: He was created specifically as an antidote for this. Bill Cosby was tired of all the father figures on TV being essentially dominated by their kids, and created a competent, intelligent, but still funny father character for himself. It's still present in a downplayed form, as the family consistently bands together to stop him from trying to do any repairs around the house.

characters.name: Clair Olivia Hanks Huxtable
characters.description: The Ace:A smart, classy, successful career woman who rarely loses an argument. Even when hearing her name years later, a college professor she had recalls how great of a student she was.Denise decides to defy this in one episode where they take a pottery class and Clair's initial attempts areless than stellar. Berserk Button:Never under any circumstances let Clair catch you in a web of lies: being an attorney she's also an expert at unraveling them and trying to further cover them up only makes things worse.Phylicia Rashād stated that Clair only truly got angry at one of the children when she feels they've squandered their potential. Sondra's not going to law school to open a wilderness store and Denise's getting married to a navy man who already has one kid are the crowning examples.Clair also had a low tolerance for her children deliberately going behind her back to do things she specifically told them not to. Shereallyblew her stack after Vanessa and her friends sneaked out to go to a concert in Baltimore and had their tickets, money, and car stolen. characters.name: Sondra Huxtable Tibideaux
characters.description: Cool Big Sis: More serious and responsible than her younger siblings. Deadpan Snarker: Inherited straight from her father. Happily Married: To Elvin starting in Season 4. Mama Bear: Sondra inherited this from her mother. "Day of the Locusts" is a more comedic example than most, but it proves that this runs in the family. She even intimidated Clair. Promotion to Opening Titles: She only shows up in a few episodes of the first season, but she is promoted to a regular character in the second season, although she is not often seen.

characters.name: Denise Huxtable Kendall
characters.description: The Bus Came Back: After beingPut on a Bus, she made a few appearances in Seasons 4 and 5 and returned as a regular character in Season 6. Cloudcuckoolander: Denise seems to have become more flighty after her return to the show. Dude Magnet: In early seasons she has a different boyfriend every episode. The Fashionista: She loves fashion, though her style is quite eccentric. Flanderization: Denise started out as a spunky, independent, intelligent young woman. Somewhere along the line, she turned into a flaky, clueless freeloader. Additionally, despite being willing to leave New York to travel to Africa for a photojournalism assignment (the actress was written out for maternity leave), she somehow freaked out at the notion of leaving New York, for the wilds of... Rhode Island.

characters.name: Theodore Aloysius "Theo" Huxtable
characters.description: Acquired Situational Narcissism: Theo gets his 15 minutes of fame after accidentally fishing up the dead body of a gangster and lets it go to his head. Vanessa quickly calls him out on the fact that he didn't actually do anything other than get lucky. Big Brother Instinct: Having four sisters, Theo exhibits this fairly often, even though two of them are older than he is. Big Eater: He gets this from Cliff, and it becomes more pronounced once he starts college. At one point, he eats four jumbo burgers and the fries that came with them in under a minute. Book Dumb: A running theme in early seasons. Character Development: From aBook Dumbunder-achiever in high school to a determined, successful college graduate.

characters.name: Vanessa Huxtable
characters.description: Bratty Teenage Daughter: Vanessa went from a smart but mischievous child to a teenager constantly pushing the boundaries of what she's allowed to wear, who she can date, where she can go, etc. The season 3 intro drives this home; Cliff does a silly dance with each family member, but when it's Vanessa's turn, she just stands there rolling her eyes (she rejoins the fun in later seasons). Can't Get Away with Nuthin': She and her friends play a drinking game that leaves them all completelyhammered, to the point that she has to call Denise for a ride home, and she pays for it in the form of a terrible hangover and throwing up in her bed. Cliff and Clair don't bother punishing her for this because she's already having a bad enough time of it. The group's next misadventure involves sneaking out of the city to see a concert in Baltimore, in which their car, tickets, and spending money are all stolen, but Clair's wrath far outstrips these disasters once she and Cliff find out. Demoted to Extra: While still listed in the starring cast, Vanessa's role was significantly reduced in the final two seasons, as she began to attend college in real life. Go-Getter Girl: She works very hard at school and gets excellent grades, ultimately earning enough credits to finish high school a year early. Hormone-Addled Teenager: Vanessa is by far the most boy-crazed of the Huxtable girls.

characters.name: Rudith Lillian "Rudy" Huxtable
characters.description: A-Cup Angst: In a later episode Rudy enters puberty but she's upset that she hasn't...developed as much as some of the other girls in her grade. The Ace: The family learns in Season 2 that she has a talent for Football and immediately becomes the team's star player despite only playing in two games before the season ends Rudy decides to move on. Adorably Precocious Child: In early seasons. The Baby of the Bunch: The "baby" of the family in early seasons before she grows up and is replaced by Olivia. Catchphrase: Rudy always tends to say, "Awww, man." when she's told to do something she doesn't want to do.

characters.name: Extended Family Members
characters.description: Cool Old Guy. Even though he's two generations separated from the Huxtable kids (or three in the case of Olivia, Nelson, and Winnie), he can easily relate to them. He readily takes to video games with a little prompting from Olivia, and he has good enough connections to get the family a stack of tickets to aMichael Jacksonconcert — eighth row center, no less. Dad the Veteran: Served in Europe during World War II. Determinator: According to one of his World War II stories, he once had an enemy pillbox dead in his sights and was waiting for the soldiers to come out so he could shoot them. They knew he was there and tried to wait him out. He held his position for so long that by the time they finally did come out, the war had ended. Embarrassing Tattoo: When he was a teenager, he decided to have Anna's name tattooed across his chest in order to show his love for her. Unfortunately, he was suffering from a cold on the day he had it done, and the congestion made his voice sound like "Adda" to the tattoo artist. Anna wasn't at all happy when she learned of this, since a girl named Adda was her main rival for Russell's affections. She insisted that he get the tattoo removed — leaving a big scar that he later told Cliff was the result of fighting off a German attack in World War II. Happily Married: To Anna.

characters.name: Friends and Neighbors
characters.description: Rudy's longtime friend. Childhood Friends: With Rudy. In later seasons, he starts being jealous of Rudy's relationship with Stanley. In-Series Nickname: Rudy nicknames him "Bud" when they first meet, but starts calling him by his real name in later season. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He is a good friend to Rudy, but also often shows a sleazy and sexist streak in his behavior. He'd almost count as aToxic Friend Influenceif Rudy wasn't sharp enough to challenge the disagreeable things he says, at least most of the time. Only One Name: We never learn his last name.
